The clearest direct evidence is the cabinet/advisory lineup itself, while the strongest negative evidence comes from broader governance and corruption reporting rather than a formal personnel review.","evidence":[{"title":"New Cabinet Formation: Loyalists, fresh faces likely to get priority","publisher":"The Daily Star","date":"January 9, 2024","url":"https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/new-cabinet-formation-loyalists-fresh-faces-likely-get-priority-3515421","summary":"Contemporaneous reporting said Hasina was expected to lean on her party core and prioritize loyalists when forming the new cabinet. This is direct evidence of a patronage-leaning selection style, though it was a preview rather than the final roster.","question_ids":["7B.5"]},{"title":"Kamal Chowdhury named education, culture advisor to Hasina, Joy returns to advise her on ICT","publisher":"bdnews24.com","date":"January 21, 2024","url":"https://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/oe9ngi5wkz","summary":"The piece says Sajeeb Wazed Joy, Hasina’s son, was reappointed as ICT adviser. That is direct family-linked staffing in a top advisory role, which weighs against a purely merit-based or impersonal appointment pattern.","question_ids":["7B.5"]},{"title":"Sheikh Hasina sworn in as PM for 5th term, forms 37-member cabinet","publisher":"BSS","date":"January 11, 2024","url":"https://b.bssnews.net/news-flash/167551","summary":"The cabinet did include two technocrats, Yeafesh Osman and Samanta Lal Sen. This is weak positive evidence that Hasina did not fill every post with pure political loyalists, but technocrats were a small minority in a broadly Awami League-dominated cabinet.","question_ids":["7B.5"]},{"title":"PM assigns charges to her 7 advisors","publisher":"The Daily Star","date":"January 21, 2024","url":"https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/pm-assigns-charges-her-7-advisors-3524926","summary":"The advisory circle included economists, academics, and a former principal secretary, which is a genuine competence signal. But it also included long-time trusted insiders such as Salman F. Rahman and Tarique Ahmed Siddique, so this is mixed evidence rather than a clean technocratic break.","question_ids":["7B.5"]},{"title":"Inclusion of govt procuring agencies in e-GP mandatory","publisher":"Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority","date":"March 6, 2024","url":"https://www.bppa.gov.bd/media-communication/news-1446.html","summary":"BPPA said e-GP was mandatory and described it as a transparency and accountability reform. This is a real competence-oriented administrative reform that reduces room for favoritism in procurement, but it is indirect evidence about governance quality, not proof of merit-based political appointments.","question_ids":["7B.5"]},{"title":"Bangladesh: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Freedom House says the Awami League consolidated power through harassment of the opposition and critical media, corruption was endemic, anticorruption enforcement was politicized, and state institutions were co-opted. This is strong negative evidence that the governing system was shaped by patronage and control rather than neutral professionalism.","question_ids":["7B.5"]},{"title":"AL govt created lawless economy, crony capitalism, captured public organizations","publisher":"The Daily Star","date":"October 31, 2024","url":"https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/al-govt-created-lawless-economy-crony-capitalism-captured-public-organizations-3741796","summary":"The white-paper lead quoted in this piece said authoritarian practices produced crony capitalism and a nexus of bureaucrats, political leaders, and business interests that captured public organizations. This is direct evidence of elite capture and self-dealing dynamics, which maps closely to the “cronies, business associates, loyalists, and yes-men” side of the lens.","question_ids":["7B.5"]}]}
